emily_r: quick repro i found for a weird HF->Redwood chat_template conversion bug — system role disappears when the jinja has invisible chars around tags.

emily_r: example template i used:

```jinja
{% if user.name %}
<|system|>Welcome {{ user.name }}\n
{% endif %}

{{ history }}
```

emily_r: when we run the conversion script (hf_chat_template_to_redwood) the final prompt ends up with the `system` line concatenated into the previous message and the leading newline is gone. looks like an invisible delimiter is breaking the sentinel split.

ravi: can you paste the raw bytes? sounds like a zero-width space (U+200B) or similar sneaking into templates from copy/paste.

emily_r: pasted raw hex around the jinja tag, found `e2 80 8b` right after the `{%` in one of the templates. so yep ZWSP.

morgan: that explains a few eval flakiness cases we saw during quant bring-up — prompts that should start with system instructions were treated as continuation tokens, quality regressed on a few instruction-following tests.

ci-bot: [automated] conversion-tests: FAIL chattemplate_render.test_system_role_preserve — saw mismatch:
```
expected: "<|system|>Welcome Alice\n"
actual:   "Welcome Alice\n"
```

ravi: theory: the sentinel detection code splits on whitespace boundaries and explicit ascii spaces. ZWSP isn't considered whitespace in python's `split()` in some places, so sentinel token becomes glued to previous token and tokenizers later don't pick it up.

sara: quick mitigation: run a normalization pass that removes any non-printable / bidi / zero-width characters before template rendering. also add explicit sentinel guards so conversion inserts separators like `\n<|system|>\n` regardless.

qa-bot: repro steps attached:
1) create jinja template with U+200B between `{%` and `%}` (copy from MS Word)
2) run `tools/hf_to_rw --chat-template path`
3) compare rendered prompt vs expected

emily_r: i'll open a small PR: 1) preprocessor to strip ZWSP + other invisible chars, 2) conversion change to always pad sentinels with `\n` on both sides, 3) add unit test in `chattemplate_render.test_system_role_preserve`.

morgan: fwiw we should also add a short fuzz test that injects random U+200B/U+2060 into templates to catch regressions.

ravi: agree. small note: when stripping, prefer normalization to replacement with space so we don't accidentally create double spaces inside inline code blocks. strip-only + sentinel-padding should be safe.

emily_r: thanks — i'll tag you on the PR and add the CI test. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: [automated] linked issue #3421 created by emily_r: "chat_template conversion: strip invisible delimiters and robust sentinel padding"
